description: Download a Eurostat dataset in bulk through the SDMX 2.1 TSV endpoint and stage it as a SQL table on the dataframe canvas — the route to a whole dataset, where eurostat_query_dataset is the route to a slice of one. The TSV wire format is roughly half the bytes of the JSON-stat body eurostat_query_dataset reads, so it reaches datasets that would otherwise time out, and it is expanded here into one row per non-blank TSV cell, including the unflagged ":" cells that mark a period a series lacks or a period of a frequency it has no observation of. Filters take the same dimension-code map eurostat_query_dataset uses and are applied server-side by Eurostat; call eurostat_get_dataset_info first for the dimension codes and eurostat_get_dimension_values for their values. Narrow with since_period/until_period rather than asking for the most recent N periods — the TSV layout keeps a column for every period whichever is requested, so a period range is what actually shrinks the response. Transfers are bounded by a decoded-byte budget enforced while streaming: complete rows within the allowed prefix are retained with budgetExceeded set; a budget too small for a usable row fails as byte_budget_exceeded with narrowing guidance. Only preview_limit rows come back inline. When a table is staged, call eurostat_dataframe_describe first to confirm its columns, then eurostat_dataframe_query; without a canvas, rows past the preview are not retained.

canvas_id.description: Reuse an existing dataframe canvas so this download lands beside earlier results and can be joined against them. Pass the canvasId a previous eurostat_download_dataset or eurostat_query_dataset response returned; omit to start a fresh canvas. Ignored on deployments without a dataframe canvas. A download that yields no row (a header-only table) fails as no_results and leaves the canvas untouched.

dataset_code.description: Dataset code (e.g., "nama_10_gdp"). Required. A DS-* code — Comext detailed trade or PRODCOM, in any case — is served by the Comext host, which refuses an unfiltered download of its large collections as extraction_too_big: filter it, including freq on the trade flows, which mix annual and monthly series.

filters.description: Dimension filters as a map of dimension code → array of accepted values, applied by Eurostat before the body is sent. Example: {"unit": ["CP_MEUR"], "na_item": ["B1G"], "geo": ["DE", "FR"]}. Omit a dimension or pass an empty array to accept every value for it; a blank or whitespace-only value is likewise unset and dropped ([""] accepts every value, ["", "DE"] is ["DE"]). A value holding "+" is split into separate values (OR): ["DE+FR"] is ["DE", "FR"]. A value holding "." is rejected as invalid_dimension before any request: no Eurostat code contains one. Dimension codes match in any case ("GEO" is geo). Do not put "time" here — use since_period/until_period. Naming a dimension the dataset does not have is rejected with the dataset's dimension list rather than silently ignored. A value Eurostat does not know fails the download as invalid_dimension; a valid value with no observation in the selected periods adds none, and the response names it in emptyValues.

preview_limit.description: How many rows to echo inline, from the start of the download. Default 25; positive integers above 500 are clamped to 500 with a notice. The full download is on the canvas table when one was staged; this is orientation, not the result set.

since_period.description: Start of the period range, inclusive, sent as startPeriod. Accepted forms: YYYY, YYYY-MM, YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY-Qn (1–4), YYYY-Sn (1–2), YYYY-Tn (1–3), YYYY-Mnn (01–12), YYYY-Wnn (a week the year has, up to 53) or YYYY-Dnnn (a day the year has, up to 366) (e.g., "2020", "2023-Q1", "2024-01"). Extra leading zeros after the letter are dropped ("2020-W001" is sent as "2020-W01"), a day of the year is sent as three digits ("2026-D1" as "2026-D001"), and YYYY-A1 is sent as YYYY. Any form works on any dataset, read as a span of days, but Eurostat keeps only periods wholly inside the range, per frequency: "2022-06" on annual data excludes 2022, which starts before the bound, and a notice names that period when the TSV header shows its frequency. A range whose first and last day are the same day is requested as that day and the next, and the next day is dropped before anything is counted or staged. A malformed or non-existent period (e.g., "2020-13") is rejected as invalid_period. The most effective way to shrink a bulk response: it removes period columns from the TSV rather than blanking their cells.

until_period.description: End of the period range, inclusive (e.g., "2024"), sent as endPeriod, in the same forms as since_period. Omit for data through the latest available period. A bound that falls inside a period excludes it here too: "2023-06" on annual data excludes 2023, which ends after the bound. The range must hold at least one day: a since_period that starts after until_period ends is rejected as invalid_period, and bounds of different frequencies are compared by day.

name: eurostat_download_dataset

absentCellCount.description: Unflagged ":" rows — obs_value null with no flag, status or text — at a period of a frequency the same series carries in another downloaded row: periods that series lacks, where Eurostat publishes no observation. Only periods inside that frequency's span count: from its first to its latest period any downloaded row has an observation in. The rows at a period before or after the span, which no downloaded row has an observation in, are counted and named in the notice instead. Unflagged rows at the periods of a frequency the series has no observation of (the padding of a mixed-frequency slice, or a series that is ":" throughout) are left out, and a flagged ":" or a text value is an observation, never counted. Part of rowCount and missingCount, and counted over the rows downloaded, so a budget-cut download counts its prefix and settles the span over it.

appliedQuery.description: The bulk request as the server built it.

filters.description: Dimension filters sent to Eurostat. A value holding "+" appears as its pieces; blank values and dimensions left with no value are dropped.

url.description: The SDMX request URL, so the download can be reproduced. A one-day range goes out as that day and the next, so its endPeriod is a day past untilPeriod.

budgetExceeded.description: True when the byte budget stopped the transfer before the dataset ended, making the rows a prefix rather than the whole thing. Narrow with filters or a period range, or raise EUROSTAT_BULK_MAX_BYTES.

bytesRead.description: Decoded TSV bytes accepted for parsing, after decompression when applicable; never more than EUROSTAT_BULK_MAX_BYTES, including an incomplete trailing line that is discarded.

canvasId.description: Dataframe canvas holding the staged download. Pass to eurostat_dataframe_describe, eurostat_dataframe_query, or a later staging call. Omitted when nothing was staged.

compressed.description: True when Eurostat sent the body gzip-compressed. It does so without a Content-Encoding header on large responses, so this reports what the stream actually carried.

dimensionsUsed.description: Dimension codes carried by the downloaded rows, in the order Eurostat keys them (e.g., ["freq", "unit", "na_item", "geo"]). Read from the TSV header, so it reflects the response rather than metadata. The period lives in the separate "time" column.

emptyValues.description: Filter values the dataset has but no downloaded row carries an observation for — no value, flag, status or text in the selected periods — keyed by filter key, spelled as sent (matching ignores case). Eurostat fails a download naming a code it does not know, so each is a valid value; it can carry data in other periods or beside other filter values. Never a period. Omitted when every filter value has an observation, and when budgetExceeded is true, since the rows not downloaded could hold any of them.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `byte_budget_exceeded`: The decoded TSV byte budget was exhausted before a complete header and usable row could be read. `not_found`: The dataset code is not available for dissemination (HTTP 404, SDMX faultcode 100). `invalid_dimension`: A filter key is not a dimension of this dataset; the error names every such key and lists the dataset's dimensions in key order; a filter value contains "." (rejected before any request); or Eurostat rejects a filter value, or the period range selects no period of the dataset (SDMX faultcode 150): it misses the coverage, or holds no whole period. The fault covers both; its TIME_PERIOD clause tells the period range apart. `filter_arity`: Eurostat rejected the positional dimension key because it carried the wrong number of positions (SDMX faultcode 140, INVALID_QUERY_NB_FILTERS), meaning the dataset structure has changed since the metadata call. `invalid_period`: since_period or until_period is not a period literal, or names a month, quarter, semester, trimester, week or day that does not exist, or since_period starts after until_period ends. Checked before any request — the bulk endpoint would otherwise roll an out-of-range period into a neighbouring one, and answer an inverted range with the whole series — and SDMX faultcode 140 TIME_PERIOD_FILTER_SPEC_INVALID maps here too. `async_queued`: Eurostat answered HTTP 200 with a SOAP syncResponse queue ticket (status SUBMITTED) instead of data, because the extraction was too costly to serve synchronously. `no_results`: The download completed but yielded no row: a header-only table, or a one-day reply whose only cells fall on the next day. Nothing is staged, and no canvas is created or touched. A table whose only rows are unflagged ":" cells succeeds with those rows, with periodRange omitted. `extraction_too_big`: Eurostat refused the extraction as too large (SDMX faultcode 413, HTTP 413): past its 5,000,000-row extraction limit, or an unfiltered download of a large DS-* Comext collection, which Eurostat serves only filtered. Covers every dataset, on either host. `upstream_fault`: The SDMX data endpoint returned a fault this server does not model, or a body that is not a TSV table; for a filtered download, the structure endpoint returned a structure this server cannot build a filter key from; the data endpoint — or, for a filtered download, the structure endpoint — answered HTTP 501, which is not retried; or it answered another HTTP 5xx or could not be reached on every retry, which the error marks retryable. `retry_deadline_exceeded`: The download did not complete within EUROSTAT_BULK_TIMEOUT_MS (120 s by default), every attempt, backoff and the streamed body included; or, for a filtered download, the structure read that orders its filter key did not answer within the request deadline. `canvas_not_found`: A canvas_id was supplied for staging but is unknown or its lifetime has elapsed. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

missingCount.description: Rows carrying no numeric value (obs_value is null): observations published without a number — a flagged ":" or a text value — and every unflagged ":" row, a period its series lacks (inside or outside the span absentCellCount counts) or a period of a frequency its series has no observation of.

notice.description: Guidance on every download: the staged table with the required eurostat_dataframe_describe then eurostat_dataframe_query sequence (or, without a canvas, what was returned inline and what was discarded), preceded by a period a bound falls inside when the TSV header shows that frequency, by byte-budget disclosure when the budget stopped the transfer, by what the unflagged ":" rows are — the rows at periods no downloaded row has an observation in, before or after a frequency's span of periods with one, counted and named per frequency; periods a series lacks inside that span (absentCellCount); the padding of a mixed-frequency slice — by the filter values with no observation (emptyValues), up to 24 named with an omitted count, and by the inline-preview length when preview_limit returns fewer rows than were downloaded.

observations.description: The first preview_limit rows of the download, in the order Eurostat streamed them. A prefix of the staged table, not a sample.

items.description: One downloaded row: one column per dimension holding its code, "time" for the period, then obs_value, obs_flag, obs_flag_label, conf_status, conf_status_label. A label column is null when Eurostat publishes no label for that code. Rows of a DS-* dataset also carry obs_value_text after obs_value: a value Eurostat published as text, such as a PRODCOM quantity unit ("KG"), kept verbatim with obs_value null; a PRODCOM ":C" arrives as conf_status "C" instead.

periodRange.description: Period coverage of the observations actually downloaded. Narrower than the dataset when budgetExceeded is true or a period range was applied.

end.description: Latest period of a row carrying an observation, read the same way as start. Omitted, with the other bound, when no row carries an observation.

start.description: Earliest period of a row carrying an observation — a value, a flag, a status or a text value; an unflagged ":" row sets no bound. Omitted, with the other bound, when no row carries an observation.

rowCount.description: Rows expanded from the download, one per non-blank cell. A row carrying a value, a flag, a status or a text value is an observation, a flagged ":" (a value Eurostat reports as unavailable) included. A row holding an unflagged ":" — obs_value null with no flag, status or text — is not: it is a period its series lacks (counted in absentCellCount when the series has an observation of that frequency and the period lies inside that frequency's span, from its first to its latest period any downloaded row has an observation in; counted in the notice when it lies outside) or a period of a frequency its series has no observation of.

stagedRowCount.description: Rows written to the canvas table. Matches rowCount. Omitted alongside tableName.

tableName.description: Canvas table holding every downloaded row. Call eurostat_dataframe_describe with canvasId first to confirm the table and columns, then eurostat_dataframe_query. Omitted when this deployment runs without a dataframe canvas, in which case only the inline preview survives the call.

totalCount.description: Rows the download produced — equal to rowCount, unflagged ":" rows included: a period their series lacks (absentCellCount inside its frequency's span of periods with an observation, the notice outside it) or a period of a frequency their series has no observation of. The inline observations array holds only the first preview_limit of them; budgetExceeded, not this count, says whether the download is the whole dataset.

title: Download Eurostat Dataset
